chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jamilah, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever conceals a testimony or testifies with it in order to shed the blood of a Muslim person, or to usurp the wealth of a Muslim person, will come on the Day of Resurrection with darkness on his face extending as far as the eye can see, and on his face will be marks of toil; the creatures will recognize him by his name and his lineage.

And whoever testifies with a true testimony in order to revive the right of a Muslim person, will come on the Day of Resurrection with light on his face extending as far as the eye can see; the creatures will recognize him by his name and his lineage.'
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not see that God, Blessed and Exalted, says: "And establish the testimony for the sake of God"?' [65:2]

key_terms.شَهَادَةَ حَقٍّ: True/rightful testimony — testimony that upholds justice and preserves the rights of others
key_terms.كَتَمَ: Concealment of testimony — a grave sin in Islamic law; suppressing knowledge of truth when called upon
key_terms.كُدُوحٌ: Marks of toil/scratches — visible signs of spiritual suffering and disgrace on the face at resurrection
key_terms.لِيَزْوِيَ: To usurp/withhold — unlawfully seizing another's property through false testimony
key_terms.مَدَّ الْبَصَرِ: Extending as far as the eye can see — an idiom indicating the immensity and expanse of the light or darkness
key_terms.يُهْدِرَ: To waste/shed blood unlawfully — causing someone's life to be forfeited through false legal proceedings

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for concealing or giving false testimony according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Baqir (AS) quoting the Prophet (SAWW), presents a vivid eschatological contrast between false/concealed testimony and truthful testimony. The false witness who betrays a Muslim's blood or wealth is condemned to face the Day of Judgment with darkness and marks of suffering permanently visible, while the truthful witness is honored with radiant light. Imam al-Baqir reinforces this by citing Quran 65:2, grounding the obligation in divine command. The hadith addresses a critical issue in early Islamic jurisprudence, as false testimony was one of the gravest social crimes threatening community justice.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, and Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who conceals a testimony, or testifies with it in order to waste by it the blood of a Muslim person, or to block the wealth of a Muslim person, would come on the Day of Judgement, and for his face would be darkness to the extent of the vision, and in his face would (signs of) toil (labour). The creatures would recognise him by his name and his lineage.

And the one who testified with a true testimony, reviving by it a right of a Muslim person, would come on the Day of Judgement, and for his face would be light to the extent of the vision. The creatures would recognise him by his name and his lineage.
Then Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Do you not see that Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying [65:2] and establish the testimony for the Sake of Allah’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran and Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from Jabir who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said this. ‘One may hide a testimony, or testify to invalidate the case of the murder of a Muslim, or to turn away from its rightful course the assets of a Muslim. He on the Day of Judgment will be brought with darkness before him as far as eyes can see, with bruises on his face whom all creatures will know by his name and genealogy.

One who presents the right testimony to revive a right of a Muslim, he on the Day of Judgment will be brought with light before him as far as the eye can see, and all creatures will know him by his name and genealogy.’
Abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Have you not seen that Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, says, ‘. . . you must present the testimony for Allah.’ [65:2]
